newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges lift on bunker demand,ignore crude.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges lift on bunker demand,ignore crude.

text.p: The European fuel barge market ignored yesterday's sharp fall in crude prices to gain value on the back of better bunker demand on Wednesday, traders said.
After early deals at $77.50 fob a tonne for high sulphur fuel barges prices jumped to $80/$81 in the ARA area.
"When trading first started people didn't realise how much bunker demand there was and they reacted to crude," said one trader. "But swaps were not so bearish and prices picked up."
High sulphur cargoes were quiet though traders were believed positioning themselves for the results of the Portugese buy tender due out today.
A slight overhang of Russian cracked material was seen in the Rotterdam market but in smaller amounts than last week.
One percent physical prices held firm, despite swaps weakening after crude futures fell. But values were largely notional given that prompt supplies are so thin.
"On the physical there is nothing happening for some time," said one trader.
Low sulphur straight-run was steady at the $104/$106 fob level it fell to after Tuesday's cargo deal out of Scandinavia done at around $105 fob a tonne.
